title: Finite-range comparison
statement: Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$. All coefficients are abelian groups: let $K\in D^+(\Ab(X_{\Et}))$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and let $a\le b$ be integers with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Write $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$, $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ and $\Ex_\square:\Phi\to\Psi$ for the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Let $\varphi$ be the spectral-sequence morphism induced by $\Ex_\square$ on the two truncation couples [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], whose spectral sequences are (2) and (3) of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations]. If $\varphi_2^{p,q}:g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ is an isomorphism for every $(p,q)$, then $\varphi_\infty^{p,q}$ and the induced map $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K}):\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$ are isomorphisms for every $(p,q)$ and every $n$. Consequently $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is an isomorphism. In the generic abelian-coefficient notation this is $\operatorname{IsIso}((\operatorname{Etale.derivedBaseChangeMapPlus}\ \Ab\ \mathsf{sq.toCommSq}).\operatorname{app}K)$, where $\mathsf{sq}:\operatorname{IsPullback}(g\prime,f\prime,f,g)$ witnesses the same square and $K$ is viewed in $\mathrm{DerivedCategory.Plus}(\mathrm{Sheaf}(X_{\Et},\Ab))$.

proof.text: Construct $t_D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\le q}K})$ and $t_E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism], both truncation couples are exact and these maps commute with all three structure maps, including the boundary. They therefore satisfy the exact-couple-morphism hypotheses of [lem-sp-couple-morphism], which gives compatible maps on every spectral-sequence page, not merely unrelated maps between entries. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism] identifies the initial components with the stated degree-$p$ exchange maps of $\mathcal H^q(K)$. Thus this constructed morphism is the $\varphi$ in the hypothesis.

source.place: Proof: the comparison of the two hypercohomology spectral sequences, constructed explicitly

proof.text: The bound $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ implies the lower bound $q<a$ required by [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment]. Apply that lemma to the two couples and the map just constructed. Its clause (1) verifies $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$ and $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p\ge0$ and $q\ge a$, exactly the half-plane hypotheses required by [lem-sp-couple-morphism]. It supplies finite canonical abutment filtrations and existing limiting pages. Clause (2) supplies the isomorphisms $\iota_n:D^{0,n}\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ and $\iota'_n:D'^{0,n}\to\mathcal H^n(\Psi K)$ carrying these finite filtrations to the image filtrations on the desired abutments. Only finitely many $q\in[a,b]$ can contribute in total degree $n$; if $n<a$, all those terms are zero.

source.place: Proof: finite filtration on each abutment and the bounds

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-page-induction] to the spectral-sequence morphism of Step 1, in the abelian category $\Ab(Y'_{\Et})$: the hypothesis supplies isomorphisms on every $E_2$ component, and Step 2 supplies the existing limiting pages. Hence every finite-page component and every $E_\infty$ component is an isomorphism. Explicitly, the page induction starts with $\varphi_2$; at a successor the componentwise inverse of $\varphi_r$ commutes with the differential because $\varphi_r d_r=d'_r\varphi_r$, so it is an inverse map of page complexes. Homology and the compatible page-to-page isomorphisms give an inverse for $\varphi_{r+1}$. The cycle and boundary subobjects defining the limiting pages are carried isomorphically by these maps. This direct page-comparison lemma has no directed-colimit hypotheses and needs no singleton-index construction.

source.place: Proof: E2 isomorphisms imply Einfinity isomorphisms

proof.text: For fixed $n$, clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment] gives $\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})\circ\iota_n$. Its clause (4) says that $u_n=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$ respects every step of the image filtrations and that its graded maps are precisely $\varphi_\infty^{p,n-p}$ under the canonical identifications. Thus $u_n$ is a morphism of the finite filtered abutments of Step 2, and all its graded maps are isomorphisms by Step 3. All hypotheses of [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] are now supplied, so $u_n$ is an isomorphism for each $n$ (no strictness hypothesis is needed).

source.place: Tag 0127 (lemma-characterize-strict), finite-filtration induction; blueprint final clause

proof.text: Every geometric-stalk functor carries the cohomology-sheaf isomorphisms $u_n$ and their inverses to inverse maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] on $Y'$ to $\Ex_{\square,K}:\Phi K\to\Psi K$, whose two objects are bounded below as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. It gives that $\Ex_{\square,K}$ itself is an isomorphism.

old_proof.text: Identify the arrow, rather than just its source and target. By [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is the composite of the unit $\eta_{f',g^{-1}Rf_*K}$, the square transport $Rf'_*\theta^D_{\square,Rf_*K}$, and the counit map $Rf'_*g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,K}$. In exact master MorphismDefs.lean, Etale.baseChange_app expands the component into baseChangeUnitStep, baseChangeSquareStep and baseChangeCounitStep. Their component formulas are respectively these same unit, square transport, and counit, with $A=\Ab$ and the commutative-square proof $\mathsf{sq.toCommSq}$. The termwise exact abelian inverse images of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] are the master's derived upper-star functors. Thus the composite equals the master component, on the same $K$, from $g^{-1}Rf_*K$ to $Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$. No $\operatorname{ModuleCat}\Lambda$ transformation is substituted. If one uses the alternate square notation of sbc-def-base-change-map, its letters must be renamed $(T,S,X,Y;g,f,e,h)=(X,Y,Y',X';f,g,g',f')$, so the old subscript would be $\operatorname{BC}_{g,f}$; the statement instead names the master arrow explicitly.

lean.statement: theorem finite_range_exchange_comparison {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) (_hK : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero ((_root_.DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) (_h₂ : ∀ p q : ℤ, IsIso (tE (derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} sq.toCommSq) K p q)) : (∃ P Q : BigradedExactCouple (Sheaf Y'.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) 0, P.D = D (truncationPhi f g) K ∧ Q.D = D (truncationPsi g' f') K ∧ ∃ hPE : P.E = E (truncationPhi f g) K, ∃ hQE : Q.E = E (truncationPsi g' f') K, HEq P.alpha (alpha (truncationPhi f g) K) ∧ HEq Q.alpha (alpha (truncationPsi g' f') K) ∧ HEq P.f (CategoryTheory.TruncationExchange.f (truncationPhi f g) K) ∧ HEq Q.f (CategoryTheory.TruncationExchange.f (truncationPsi g' f') K) ∧ HEq P.g (CategoryTheory.TruncationExchange.g (truncationPhi f g) K) ∧ HEq Q.g (CategoryTheory.TruncationExchange.g (truncationPsi g' f') K) ∧ ∃ L : LimitSubobjects P, ∃ M : LimitSubobjects Q, ∃ z : ∀ p q : ℤ, (L.Z p q : Sheaf Y'.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ⟶ (M.Z p q : Sheaf Y'.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}), ∃ tInf : ∀ p q : ℤ, P.pageInfinity L p q ⟶ Q.pageInfinity M p q, (∀ p q : ℤ, z p q ≫ (M.Z p q).arrow = (L.Z p q).arrow ≫ eqToHom (congrFun (congrFun hPE p) q) ≫ tE (derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} sq.toCommSq) K p q ≫ eqToHom (congrFun (congrFun hQE p) q).symm) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (limitBoundary_le_cycle P L p q)) ≫ tInf p q = z p q ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (limitBoundary_le_cycle Q M p q))) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, IsIso (tInf p q))) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, IsIso ((_root_.DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ n).map ((derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} sq.toCommSq).app K))) ∧ IsIso ((derivedBaseChangeMapPlus AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} sq.toCommSq).app K)
